name: frame_survey
description: Look at EVERY frame of a video: numbered contact sheets with the frame number and time on each tile, a change score that makes a short run of differing frames stand out without a scene cut, a range of frames at native size, and a checked repair of an MP4 or AVI that will not open. THE DECODER is ffmpeg (5.1 or later for -fps_mode; an older one is given -vsync 0), with ffprobe for the stream's shape, run as programs: this tool has no decoder of its own, and where ffmpeg or ffprobe is not on PATH every mode answers status failed with that reason in one JSON document (repair still prints the container's diagnosis, which needs no decoder). RULES (they are in every answer and in every refusal too): (1) Survey first, with the default call ({"video": ...}): every frame is decoded, tiled with its frame number and time, and scored. Read `runs` before the sheets: a run is a stretch of frames in which one region changed and changed back (a caption, an overlay, a flash) with no scene cut, and it names the sheets that show it. (2) A sampled or capped survey is `partial` and says what it skipped (every, max_frames, the clock): a run shorter than the sampling step can fall between two samples, so "nothing stands out" is a negative only for a `complete` survey with every: 1. (3) Take the frames a run names at native size ({"mode": "extract", "first": N, "last": M}) before reading text off a tile: a tile is a reduced copy. Frame numbers count decoded frames of the first video stream from 0; a time is the frame's own presentation time when the decoder gave one, else frame / rate, and the answer says which. (4) A file that will not open goes to {"mode": "repair"}: it says what the container lacks (an MP4's moov, a cut mdat, an AVI's index), writes a remuxed copy, and counts the frames that copy DECODES. The count decoded is the claim; a missing moov with no second file from the same recorder is not rebuilt, and the answer says so. SURVEY (the default): the first video stream is decoded once, each frame reduced to a tile (tile_width, default 160) on a pipe; tiles go left to right, top to bottom, columns x rows a sheet (default 10 x 6), on sheet-0001.png onward, each with its frame number and time (a 3 x 5 pixel font of the tool's own); frames.tsv has one row a decoded frame (frame, time, where the time came from, score) and windows.tsv one a window. THE SCORE of a frame is the share of 32 x 18 blocks whose mean moved by more than 8 of 255 from the frame decoded before it: a scene cut changes half of the blocks or more at once (scene_cuts); a local change (a caption, an overlay, a flash, an object entering) changes few. A RUN is a pair of local changes over the same region with no cut between them, the first when the region changed and the second when it changed again: first_frame to last_frame, the region in native pixels and the sheets that show it. It is a candidate, from block means alone: steady motion in one region, or noise above the step, can make one, and a change that covers half the picture is a cut, not a run; what a run shows is read from the frames (extract). A local change is paired with the first matching one among the next 400 local changes, within 2,000 decoded frames; one without a partner is listed apart, and the pairing has 10 seconds of its own (past them the answer is partial and says from which frame). windows_that_stand_out ranks windows (window frames each, default 10) by their highest score against the clip's own median. every: N samples one frame in N and max_frames (default 20000) caps the frames decoded; either makes the answer partial with skipped and, for a cap or the clock, the start_frame to go on from. EXTRACT: frames first to last (at most 300 a call) at native size as PNG, each with its sha256 and time. TIMES: the frame's own presentation time, read from the decoder's showinfo line, when the decoder gave one, else frame / rate; times says how many of each. REPAIR: the container is read first, without a decoder (an MP4's top-level boxes: moov missing, moov at end, a box cut by the end of the file, fragments; an AVI's chunks: the RIFF or movi list cut, idx1 missing or broken), then ffmpeg remuxes what its demuxer reads (streams copied, no frame re-encoded; an MP4 with its moov in front, an AVI with a new index) into repaired.mp4 or repaired.avi, and the copy's first video stream is decoded to nothing and its frames counted. rebuilt and could_not say what was and was not rewritten; claim gives the two counts (the original's and the copy's); the count decoded is all that is verified, not that the frames are the scene's, in order, or all there were. A file with no moov box is NOT rebuilt (its sample tables and codec configuration are not in it, and no reference-file repair is run): failed, with could_not. A copy that decodes no frame is failed, never a repair. Files go to a new directory under $OUT (outside a job, under work/<agent>/tool-output); the repaired copy is written there by ffmpeg itself, the sheets and frames by this tool. Status: complete when the decoder ended cleanly at the end of the stream and every frame it gave was tiled and scored (the container's own frame count is printed beside the decoder's; the decoder's is what was read); partial for a sample, a cap, the clock, a damaged stream (a non-zero exit code, or any line the decoder wrote about an error, a corrupt or missing packet or a concealed frame while it decoded, whatever its exit code: decoder_said has the first three) or a file that could not be written; a program that left a process behind makes it partial too (program_group; on a host that cannot adopt orphans, such as macOS, every call that ran the decoder is partial for that reason alone). Bounds: frames of up to 8192 x 4320, 200,000 frames a call, the clock (max_seconds, default 540, at most 570; the manifest's timeout is 600) read for every frame. Measured with Python 3.12 and ffmpeg 9.0 on an Apple M-series host: a 320 x 180 MPEG-4 clip of 150 frames surveyed in 0.4 s; 3,000 frames of 1280 x 720 H.264 in 4.1 s (about 730 frames a second, 50 sheets); a job VM may be several times slower. Paths are printed as given; the decoder's own error lines are printed (they can quote a stream's metadata). A stop signal ends it with one JSON answer (failed, interrupted), exit 128 + the signal; the decoder is ended with it and a file that was begun is removed.

mode.description: survey (default: contact sheets and change scores), extract (frames first to last at native size) or repair (diagnose the container, write a remuxed copy, count the frames it decodes)

every.description: survey: decode one frame in this many (default 1: every frame). More than 1 makes the answer partial: a run shorter than this can fall between two samples

start_frame.description: survey: begin at this frame number (default 0); use the number a capped or clock-limited answer names to go on

max_frames.description: survey: the most frames decoded in this call (default 20000, at most 200000); a cap that is reached makes the answer partial

tile_width.description: survey: the width of a tile in pixels (default 160, 64 to 480); the height keeps the frame's shape

columns.description: survey: tiles in a row of a sheet (default 10, 1 to 20)

rows.description: survey: rows of a sheet (default 6, 1 to 20)

window.description: survey: frames in one window of windows.tsv (default 10, 2 to 1000)

first.description: extract: the first frame number to write

last.description: extract: the last frame number to write (default: first; at most 300 frames a call)

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 540, 5 to 570; the manifest's timeout is 600)
